 Hamilton High School Principal Brad Gooding submitted this report to the Hamilton School Board on Oct. 21.
 Enrollment: Seniors — 37, Juniors — 56, Sophomores — 35, Freshmen — 47, Total — 175.
 September and October Positive Office Referrals
 The following students received a Positive Office Referral from a teacher or staff member at HHS during the months of September and October: Hannah Dobbins, Khyli Hopp (2), Sophie Stromberg, Abigail Shuman (2), Annaston Swisegood, Ethan Esterday (2), Ryan Bolton (2), Killian Todd, Journee Pierce, Allison Johnson, Benton Boley, Jorge Hernandez (2), Steven Hildebrand-Selvog (2), Kami Osbon (2), Eli Carel, Cale Cunningham, Kage Kohlmorgan, Will Schlatter, Marlee Schulte, Karsyn Hobby, Sevin McTavish, Kaylee Latham, Tucker Stevens (2), Benton Boley (2), Liam Shuman, Suprince Sampson, Kara Neumann. DREAMS!
 HHS Odds and Ends
 The Wren House September Students of the Month were freshman Ashton Clark, sophomore Jordan Bretz, junior Kage Kohlmorgan, and senior Kady Combs. Each received a gift card to Wren House.
 The Marine Bank Senior of the Month for September (Fine Arts) was Roland Bouchard. He received a cash award from Marine Bank and will have the opportunity for a larger scholarship award at the end of the year.
 Jostens was here on Wednesday, Sept. 30 to meet with the class of 2029 about ordering class rings and letterman jackets. They returned on Thursday, Oct. 8 to take orders. Items will be delivered in December.
 FAFSA Night for Hamilton High School will be Thursday, Oct. 29 at Warsaw High School at 6 p.m. There is a link in the announcements for students to create a FAFSA account. Hopefully our students and parents will take advantage of this opportunity.
 Ms. Johnson and Mrs. Kohlmorgan took the environmental science students out on the river on Friday, Oct. 2 to check on the habitat of the turtles, and then again to the Keokuk dam on Tuesday, Oct. 20 to shock fish.
 The following are representing Hamilton High School in the University of Illinois Youth Leadership Academy: Niko de Guzman, Emma Henson, Laney Pfeiferling, Addison Pfeiferling, Brynlee Smeltser and Kaitlyn Starr. The first session of Youth Leadership Academy was Friday, Oct. 2. During the kickoff, students participated in the Real Colors personality assessment, learning how different personality types communicate and interact. In the afternoon they took part in team-building activities led by Mindy Pheiffer, program director at WIU’s Horn Field Campus. The next session will be Friday, Nov. 6.
 The annual Career/College Fair was held on Wednesday, Oct. 7. There were 37 entities in attendance – 18 colleges/universities, 16 careers and three branches of the military. Thank you to those institutions, businesses and military branches for coming to share with our students what they have to offer. Students from Illini West and Warsaw also came and there were about 235 students in attendance. The representatives were very impressed with the questions and investigations from all the students. Mr. Taylor is receiving positive feedback from both presenters and students.
 Congratulations to senior Dante Patch of West Hancock on his fourth place WCC Cross County all conference finish. This is Dante’s second consecutive all-conference finish.
 Mr. Hartweg and Ms. Cheney will be taking the following students to the FFA National Convention running Oct. 21-24: Tira Horton, Abbie Gunning, Emma Henson, Mady Bolton, Brynlee Smeltser, Sevin McTavish, Karsyn Hobby, Faith Fountain, Parker Fountain, Roland Bouchard, Kaitlyn Starr and Niko de Guzman.
 The “Double Lunch” and Game Show Friday for the month of October will be on Friday, Oct. 23. “Double Lunch” means there will be no study hall for any students that day. Students will be able to eat lunch and then visit in the cafeteria, library or one of the gyms, or play volleyball, basketball or walk in the gyms. We will use the 2:15 p.m. bell schedule and at 2:15 p.m. enjoy Family Feud in the gym. “Come on, let’s play the feud.”
 The PSAT/National Merit Scholarship Qualifying Test will be held on Monday, Oct. 26 here at Hamilton High School. Six students signed up to take the test. The test is a way for students to achieve scholarship dollars from colleges and universities.
 Student Council is currently working on plans for Red Ribbon Week, Oct. 26-30. The capstone to the week will be the Resource Fair on Friday, Oct. 30. A number of professionals and agencies will be on campus to share with the students on how they can stay in the right frame of mind.
 Jostens will be on campus on Monday, Nov. 2 to meet with the class of 2027 about ordering graduation items. They will return on Tuesday, Nov. 10 to take orders.
